title: Created an AI-powered short interactive mystery game
author: Birthday_Euphoric
selftext:
Some players gave feedback that the usual cases on the platform are quite complicated or takes too long so I am now experimenting with a shorter interactive mystery game format. 

  
Please let me know your feedback! (planning to make this a daily thing like Wordle): [https://thelastquestion.io/quick](https://thelastquestion.io/quick)

  
The Last Question is a game I solo developed 2 months ago, now with 4K+ players!

comments.author: Robonotes1760
comments.body: The premise was somewhat hard to understand, and most of my messages were spent trying to understand what I was doing and why.

replies.author: Birthday_Euphoric
replies.body: Thank you for the feedback! I am improving the tutorial/guide as I think most people will skim through the How to Play popup haha. I will be adding a bit more detailed tutorial for first time players in the new case engine I am developing!

replies.author: promptling
replies.body: If most players skim How to Play, I would make the first case teach through one tiny forced choice instead of adding more text. Then ask players to explain the goal in their own words before the second clue appears. Their answers will show what the interface taught and what still depends on instructions. I am building [Patchloop](https://patchloop.io/) for agentically built games in progress and focused playtest loops. The daily mystery format seems perfect for quick onboarding tests.

replies.author: Birthday_Euphoric
replies.body: That makes sense! Personally, I don't like those tutorial but I should definitely add this feature and then allow players to skip if they want to.
